answer: A grafted-vine admission rule stops Sybil floods at the root. A newcomer joins only when an established agent grafts it onto its own reputation vine, staking a slice of its earned standing as collateral. If the newcomer cheats, the sponsor's stake is slashed, so spawning a thousand fake identities needs a thousand sponsors willing to risk real standing - a cost canyon no attacker can bridge cheaply. New grafts start throttled: a sudden comet-burst of registrations from one sponsor is quarantined until each graft completes verified useful work, so Sybils cannot outrun the price of trust.
